newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end off lows, focus on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end off lows, focus on Wall St.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.935 -0.055 Gold NY 339.35 Lon fix 338.00
AUD US$0.7597 (Mon $0.7513) CRB Index cl 241.25 +0.73
*Stocks ended down but off their lows as investors eyed a possible Dow recovery later today. Total volume 339.1 million, value A$779.3 million, 1,239 stocks traded, 361 steady, 268 up, 610 down.
The Australian share market closed weaker on Tuesday but off its lows as investors factored in a potential Wall Street recovery later on Tuesday after the Dow pulled back 192 points on Monday.

The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended 17.9 points lower at 2,688.4, after touching an intra-day low of 2,672.5. The June share price index fell 28 points to 2,691 and at a 2.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Dealers said institutions were reluctant to sell ahead of Australia's financial year end on June 30 and used today's correction to top up portfolios.
The local bond market also finished off its lows after the Japan's Prime Minister Hashimoto clarified comments he made on Monday which triggered the Dow sell-off.
Dealers said another positive factor was that the Australian share market has been more cautious than its U.S. counterpart.
"Our market is at lofty levels but it certainly hasn't had the exponential rise we have seen on Wall Street recently," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at broker Ord Minnett.
Gale said he would be relieved rather than agitated if the Dow experienced another 200 point fall on Tuesday because a healthy correction for the Wall Street market was overdue.
Once again resource issues fared worse than industrials with Australia's largest listed company, The Broken Hill Pty Co continuing to drift ahead of its year results announcement on Friday.
BHP shares closed 10 cents weaker at A$19.40. The company's peer Rio Tinto proved to be much more resilient on the day, its stock ending 10.4 cents firmer at A$22.554.

Chemical group ICI Australia continued its strong rise as investors factored in its new status as a takeover target after its outgoing U.K. parent said on Monday it would be prepared to pass control to another company at the right price.
ICI shares ended 40 cents firmEr at A$13.00 on thin volume after adding 20 cents on Monday.
One of the most active stocks was newspaper group John Fairfax with New Zealand investment group Brierley Investments seen by dealers as the main buyer.
Fairfax shares ended 10 cents weaker at A$3.15 while the stock of potential suitor, Publishing and Broadcasting (PBL) rose 11 cents to A$7.63.
In the past week, PBL has risen on thin volume but dealers were unsure whether this was because the company was no longer a likely bidder for Fairfax or for some other reason.
In other markets, Australian bond yields finished below the day's highs helped by a clarification by Japan's Prime Minister Hashimoto about comments made on Monday.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds ended at 7.05 percent, up 0.05 percentage points on Monday's close.
The Australian dollar continued its slow motion rally Tuesday as it added a few more ticks on the day but again failed to clear key resistance.
By 5.45 p.m (0745 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7523/28 from an early US$0.7530/35 after Monday's late US$0.7510/15.
